h: Accepting Divine Kingship Brings Rest and the Promise of Freedom

p: "And You did not give it to the nations of the lands, etc."
the gift of Shabbos is for Yisrael alone
and a gentile who keeps Shabbos is liable
implying that the resting of Shabbos
depends on the covenant of milah
אַךְ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קח, א) אִיתָא
But in the holy Zohar (on this parshah, III 108a) it says:
who has the holy mark upon him
And this is as stated in the holy Zohar
that he is from the side of Cham,
That is, according to the opinion
אוֹ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם קח, ב)
or according to what is stated (ibid. 108b)
that he cohabited in the Ark,
and this was for them a forbidden relation,
since it was forbidden to them in the Ark;
And this is what it says:
"Just as Shabbos is the rest of everything,
it is the rest of spirit and body."
That is, of Yisrael it is written (Yeshayahu 60:21):
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק א קפב, ב)
Tzedek is Malchus, as is known
And this is what it says:
that one who has the holy mark
"What is the yoke of the kingship of Heaven?
on which they place a yoke, etc.,
to bring out of it good for the world, etc.,
to take upon himself the yoke
and this is the kingship of Heaven."
since Shabbos is the middah of Malchus,
which is the yoke of the kingship of Heaven,
that one who accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingship of Heaven
Is not a yoke the opposite of rest?
אַךְ הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
But it is as written several times
"They shall rejoice in Your kingship, etc.":
that it is like what is stated
"My joy is from within my fear";
in accepting the yoke of the kingship of Heaven,
the opposite of the yoke of this world.
let the children of Tziyon exult in their King."
And such a one has rest.
Not so one who blemishes his bris,
as stated (in the holy Zohar III 111a).
"And in the seventh he shall go free";
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה)
(as Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory, wrote).
implying even without the yoke of the kingship of Heaven,
even though he has not repaired the blemish
for which he was sold as a slave;
which is the middah of Malchus,
only as a name for the nations
And even a person who is more blemished
and does not want to go out
nevertheless at Yovel he goes out,
for then it is the aspect of the great shofar,
"And those lost in the land of Ashur shall come"
that is, even though they assimilated
to the point that they said (Yevamos 16b):
we take his betrothal into account,
lest he be from the Ten Tribes"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל
he will be aroused and come.
"And those cast away in the land of Egypt"
that is, one who knows that he is a Jew,
and nevertheless were surrounded by klipah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עַל הַפָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים ד, לד)
"a nation from the midst of a nation"
inside the womb of an animal, etc.
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא מוּקָּף כָּל כָּךְ בִּקְלִיפָּה
And one who is so surrounded by klipah
for him even Yovel does not help.
And this is what it says:
it is the rest of spirit and body
while on Shabbos it is the rest of everything,
and through it one can merit
